title: USB 2.0 high-speed capable device: chirp speed detection, SOF frame / microframe tracking, NRZI / bit stuffing / EOP on dp-dm, CRC5 / CRC16, ACK / NAK / STALL, DATA0/1 toggles, EP0 control (device and device_qualifier descriptors, SET_ADDRESS, SET/GET_CONFIGURATION, a vendor preset) and an EP1 interrupt-IN counter

fields.desc: high speed: set by a successful chirp handshake, cleared by the next bus reset
frame number of the last good SOF
SOFs seen with this frame number, minus 1 (the microframe in high speed)

irqs.name: RXERR
irqs.desc: token or data packet with a bad CRC5 / CRC16 or a bit-stuffing error. Held in the core until the next good token addressed to the device, so the bit is set again on every clock until then

notes: dp / dm (bidirectional tri-state pads: D+ needs the device pull-up, D- the host pull-down) pass through unchanged. One USB bit time is 4 PCLK clocks; the chirp handshake is a scaled digital model (device chirp K 64 PCLK, host chirps of at least 16 PCLK within 512 PCLK).
Enumeration and endpoint traffic run over the USB bus only; the registers report the speed, SOF tracking and receive errors.
